text:
The aftermath was in some ways worse than the ceremony itself, because it went on for so long and because I couldn't tell anyone.

The certainty that I would never have a child stayed. Rationally I knew that the trip couldn't predict anything about my fertility, but the feeling was so deep that I couldn't shake it. Every month, when my period came, it felt like confirmation. I stopped believing the doctors when they said there was still a good chance. I became withdrawn and listless, and I started to dread the fertility appointments that I used to approach with hope.

Worse was the belief that I was poisonous to children. I'm a teacher, and for months I struggled to be in the classroom. I'd look at the children and see their faces turning grey, the way they did in the trip. I'd feel a wave of nausea and have to leave the room. I avoided hugging them or touching their shoulders, which I'd always done naturally. I felt like a danger to them. I know now this was intrusive thinking, but at the time I thought it might be true. I didn't tell anyone because I was terrified someone would think I was actually dangerous.

I had panic attacks, especially at night and before work. I had nightmares about empty wombs and grey plains. I had a constant tightness in my belly.

My relationship with my husband suffered badly. I couldn't explain why I was so distant. He thought I was angry with him about the infertility. We stopped having sex, which of course also stopped our attempts to conceive. He suggested couples therapy, and I refused because I was afraid of what I'd have to say.

After about four months I took sick leave from school. I told my doctor I was burnt out. That was partly true. I spent most days on the sofa, staring at the wall. I had thoughts that my husband would be better off with someone else, someone who could give him children and wasn't poison.

The turning point came when my husband found me crying in the bathroom one evening and refused to leave until I told him everything. I did. He held me for a long time. Then he made the appointments.
Seitdem hasse ich Silvester. Ich verbringe den Jahreswechsel in einem abgelegenen Ferienhaus, weit weg vom Feuerwerk. Laute Knalle lassen mich das ganze Jahr über zusammenzucken.
Sad about nature for a few days, then fine. Made me appreciate life more.

For months after the retreat I had intrusive images of being torn apart, especially when I was falling asleep. I'd jolt awake feeling teeth in my flesh. I developed a fear of dogs and large birds, which was difficult because I live in the countryside. I had panic attacks out of nowhere. I felt disconnected from my body, like it wasn't really mine, like it was something that had been put back together and didn't quite fit.

Because the facilitators had called it an honour, I thought I was supposed to feel grateful and enlightened. When I didn't, I felt I'd failed the initiation. I became depressed and ashamed. It was almost a year before a friend who is a psychologist told me that what I was describing sounded like trauma, not initiation.
Ich war danach ein paar Wochen lang verunsichert und hatte Angst, dass ich vergesse, wer ich bin. Ich habe mir meinen Namen manchmal auf die Hand geschrieben. Dann hat sich das gelegt.

For months I had a problem with 'reality checking'. I'd wake up in the morning and not be sure if I was really awake. I'd pinch myself, check clocks, look at text. If something seemed slightly off, I'd panic that I was back in the loop. I had derealisation and a lot of anxiety. Dreams became frightening because I couldn't always tell them apart from waking life. It slowly faded over about a year.
I felt terrible guilt about my grandmother. I couldn't visit her for months, and she died before I went back. That has stayed with me.

Nach dieser Nacht ging es mir lange Zeit sehr schlecht. Die Trauer um meine Frau hat sich mit den Bildern aus dem Krankenhaus vermischt, die ich während der Erfahrung so deutlich gesehen habe. Ich hatte nachts Flashbacks, in denen ich ihr Atmen höre. Ich konnte ihre Sachen nicht mehr anschauen, ohne Schuldgefühle zu bekommen, und habe vieles in Kisten gepackt. Ich hatte immer wieder den Gedanken, dass ich ihr folgen sollte. Meine Tochter hat sich große Sorgen gemacht und hat mich oft besucht. Ich habe mich sehr zurückgezogen, nicht mehr gekocht, kaum noch gegessen. Erst mit Hilfe konnte ich da wieder herausfinden.
Wary of my usual dose for a while. Some anxiety when feeling unwell. Otherwise fine.

That day brought back a flood of combat memories that I'd kept locked away for years. I had nightmares again, which I hadn't had since leaving the army. Helicopters overhead would make me freeze. Seeing blood, even a small cut, would put me back in the compound. I became irritable and jumpy, and I started drinking more than I should. I also felt guilty about my brother, as if I'd failed him, even though I'd treated his hand properly. My wife said I seemed far away for months.
Ein paar Wochen lang hatte ich Angst, wenn mich jemand angeschrien hat. Inzwischen ist das vorbei.

The 14 lost hours haunted me. I didn't know what had happened to me. Had I been hurt? Had I done something? I was afraid to find out. For months I had panic attacks whenever I couldn't account for my time, even a few minutes. I developed derealisation, especially in crowds, and an intense fear of fractal patterns, which is annoying because they're everywhere, in trees, in carpets. I couldn't listen to electronic music. I was depressed for the rest of the year and dropped out of my course. I felt like I'd lost a piece of myself in that field.
Nervous around dogs for a while, not a big deal.

Ich hatte danach monatelang das Gefühl, dass sich etwas um meinen Hals legt, vor allem nachts. Ich konnte keine Schals oder Rollkragenpullover mehr tragen. Ich hatte Panikattacken mit Atemnot. Ich war beim HNO-Arzt, der nichts gefunden hat.
